title: Kunumi X Matter at ICLR 2026
excerpt: Taking Brazilian AI to the biggest stage in machine learning — an OOH and event experience built for a scientific audience that distrusts marketing.

body.text: Before it is a conference, ICLR is a room. A room where the people building the next decade of machine learning gather — and where marketing, in its usual costume, is not welcome.

For Kunumi, Brazil’s pioneering AI company, we designed an out-of-home and event experience that speaks the room’s language: precise, restrained, confident. No slogans shouting over the science. Presence, not promotion.

The system extends Kunumi’s brand into the city and into the venue — a sequence of statements about intelligence, matter and meaning that reads like the beginning of a conversation rather than the end of a pitch.
ICLR 2026 — OOH + Event Experience. Created by MATTER for Kunumi.

title: Living With It, A Matter Report On The Future Of Technology As Life
excerpt: What CES 2026 told us about technology settling into daily life — and what that settlement demands from brands.

body.text: Executive Summary

CES 2026 revealed technology moving closer to routine, memory, and presence. The show was less about spectacle and more about settlement: devices that want to live with people rather than perform for them. Adoption remains uneven, shaped by tolerance rather than fascination.
What Is It Really About

The industry keeps saying intelligence. What it means is intimacy. The interfaces that mattered this year were the ones that disappeared — ambient sensing, on-device memory, assistants that wait instead of interrupting. Technology is negotiating its place in the household, and the household is negotiating back.
What Felt Genuinely Exciting

Hardware with manners. Systems that forget on purpose. Accessibility features graduating into mainstream design. And a generation of products that treat attention as something to be protected, not extracted — a thesis we have been building this company on.
The Challenges

Trust remains the bottleneck. Every ambient device is a promise about data, and most brands are not yet fluent in making that promise credibly. The gap between demo and daily life is still wide — and the cost of crossing it is paid in patience, not launches.
The Wins and Highlights

The clearest wins belonged to brands that under-promised: products that named their limits, interfaces that showed their seams, companies that treated repair and longevity as features. Restraint, it turns out, demos well.
The Underwhelms
AI as a sticker. Screens where no screen was needed. The persistent confusion of novelty with progress. If a product’s story requires the word ‘revolutionary’, it usually isn’t.
What This Means For Marketers Right Now

The brands that win the ambient era will be the ones people allow into their routines. That permission is earned with presence — consistent, useful, quiet — not with reach. Plan for tolerance. Design for the hundredth use, not the first impression.
The Closing Note
CES 2026 revealed technology moving closer to routine, memory, and presence. Adoption remains uneven, shaped by tolerance rather than fascination.
The next phase will be decided by how technology settles into daily life. That settlement will be slow, negotiated, and largely invisible. This is the work ahead.

title: Matter Into Sound 06, An On-Going Series: With Guest Louise Freshel
excerpt: Matter into Sound is born from a simple truth: before image, before words, before interface, there is rhythm.
intro: Matter into Sound is born from a simple truth: before image, before words, before interface, there is rhythm. Music is pure presence. It shapes mood, memory, gesture; it reveals what doesn’t fit inside decks or processes.

body.text: A playlist suspended between digital nostalgia and sun-faded romance. Soft-focus electronics, warm basslines, drifting synths and understated groove. Music that feels slightly futuristic and strangely sentimental at the same time, somewhere between late-night drives, faded coastlines, tropical air and quiet optimism. Organic textures and analog warmth meet progressive rhythms, digital patterns and emotional soundscapes. Melodies that feel mathematical but deeply human.

For the strange intimacy of dancing with your own thoughts, of turning a sunset, a living room or an empty street into a temporary inner landscape. For the private anticipation before the atmosphere materializes into other people. Music that follows the emotional rhythm of life, melancholy and euphoria, movement and stillness.
Slow movement for fast lives.
Curated by @louisewfreshel

title: Manuel Nogueira On Shots: Craft, Silence And Leadership
excerpt: Our founder on why the seniors do the work, what the machine can’t choose, and the discipline of staying quiet until the work speaks.

body.text: In conversation with Shots, Manuel Nogueira talks about building a presence system instead of an agency — why MATTER took the pyramid out and put instruments in its place, and what that changes for clients and for the people making the work.

The machine is the strongest colleague we have ever worked with and the worst leader we could follow. It calculates, and calculating is not choosing. Choosing needs a body, a history, something at stake.

On leadership, Nogueira is direct: nothing ships that a person didn’t stand behind by name. The person who made something is credited next to it. Nobody’s exhaustion is our business model. No one’s career is our margin.
Most work now could have come from anywhere. Ours couldn’t. We leave the fingerprints on.
Full interview at Shots. Photography: MATTER Sessions.

title: Matter Into Energy, What We Care About And How Do We Do It
excerpt: The operating framework behind the work: presence and commitment, the beauty of process, radical collaboration, energy as essence.

body.text: Presence and Commitment
Be here, fully. In an age of distraction, attention is power. We choose to pay attention to what matters, to move with intention, to create from the ground up. No shortcuts.
The Beauty of Process

Transformation is not a straight line. It’s an excavation, a layering, a constant shedding of what no longer serves. We embrace the unpolished, the unfinished, the work in progress. This is where real change takes root.
Radical Collaboration

We don’t believe in hierarchy for hierarchy’s sake. The best work emerges when we all have skin in the game. This is collaboration as a shared risk, a collective pursuit, a trust in each other’s strengths.
Energy as Essence

Beyond product, beyond service—our core is energy. The drive to create, the spark of connection, the fire of curiosity. It’s about tapping into what makes us feel alive, what makes us human, and infusing that into everything we touch.

title: New Matter Drop Of Radical Collaboration
excerpt: This is the time of presence. The new drop turns the manifesto into matter — printed, stitched, worn.

body.text: Merch, for us, is the manifesto made wearable. The new drop carries the operating framework onto fabric: The Beauty of Process. Radical Collaboration. Energy as Essence.
In an era where everything is abstracted, there is an urgent need to return to the fundamentals — to affirm why matter matters and why embodied existence is essential. This is the time of presence.
Drop 01 — available soon. Follow @matterandenergy.

title: Echoes: Le Nomad — The Madrid Premiere
